title: I Printed the Dating-App Screenshot He Sent to My Coworkers

parts.text: I was in the copy room at 11:18 when three Slack DMs arrived with the same screenshot: my dating profile, circled waist-up, captioned guess who. The sender was Miles from sales, who I had matched with on Thursday and unmatched on Friday after he asked my salary. I was twenty-five. The profile photo was a hiking picture, not a crime. Miles walked past the glass and winked. I saved the DMs. I also saved his profile, where he had listed team lead even though he was an individual contributor. I printed the screenshot packet, including the salary ask. HR's door was closed. I left a copy under it labeled workplace distribution of a private profile. Then Miles posted the same photo in the random channel with a poll: dateable or coworker.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He put a poll in the public channel after already DMing the screenshot around.

social.video_title: He sent my dating profile around the office — Part 1/2
social.description: Copy room, three identical DMs, and a sales wink. Then he made it a poll. Would you have gone to HR immediately?

parts.text: HR asked Miles if he had distributed private images. He said it was a joke. The poll had forty votes. Jokes with forty votes are still distribution. They made him delete it, take a training, and stop using the hiking photo in decks. I did not want a town hall. I wanted the DMs to stop. They stopped. I kept the hiking photo on the app and took Miles off every possible algorithm. The copy room still smells like toner. I print invoices there. I do not print my face. Miles eats lunch in his car. The poll is gone. The salary question is still a no.

social.video_title: Forty votes did not make it a joke — Part 2/2
social.description: HR, a deleted poll, and training he did not want. Was a wink ever consent?
